footer: Catenta — on-chain dental passport · a neutral registry between competing actors

connect.title: On-chain dental passport
connect.subtitle: Traceability of custom-made devices, from the material lot to placement in the mouth.

what.1: One passport per prosthesis — non-transferable, with traits frozen at manufacturing.
what.2: Material lots traced and burned in the very transaction that mints the passport.
what.3: Every act timestamped and attributed to an approved actor, never rewritable afterwards.
what.4: No patient data on-chain — a salted commitment, never an identity.

roles.3: Regulator — full read access to the registry.
roles.4: No role — read-only access; on a public chain everything is readable anyway.

connect.wrongChain: Your wallet is on another network. Switch to {chain} to continue.
connect.notConfigured: The LifecycleModule address is missing: set VITE_LIFECYCLE_ADDRESS in the .env file, then reload.

lots.title: Material lots
lots.subtitle: One id per lot, a consumable quantity — burned at manufacturing.
lots.quantityHint: In the laboratory's own unit — grams, pieces, whatever: consistency is what matters.
lots.readOnly: Only an approved laboratory can declare a lot. You are browsing the registry read-only.

passports.title: Passports
passports.subtitle: One token = one device. Non-transferable, except through an accepted handoff.
passports.formSubtitle: Material is burned in the very transaction that creates the passport: the link cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
passports.noLot: No lot available: declare one first.

passport.subtitle: Timestamped, attributed, and never rewritable.

manufactured.title: Manufactured
manufactured.desc: The laboratory issued the passport by consuming material from its lot.

certified.title: Certified
certified.desc: The practitioner validated the conformity check on reception.

placed.title: Placed
placed.desc: The device is in the mouth and bound to a patient by a salted commitment.

passport.commitmentHint: Salted fingerprint: without the salt kept off-chain, it points to nobody. Erasing the patient record makes it permanently unusable.
passport.handoffHint: Must be an approved laboratory or practitioner. They will have to accept: nobody can be forced to hold a passport.
passport.nothingToDo: No action is open to you on this passport at this stage.

commitment.identityHint: This value NEVER leaves your browser. Only its salted fingerprint goes on-chain.
commitment.saltWarning: Store this salt with the patient record, in your usual system. Without it the on-chain commitment points to nobody — which is exactly what makes the right to erasure compatible with the immutability of the chain.
commitment.fileNote: Catenta salt — keep with the patient record. Without this salt the on-chain commitment is unusable.

hint.file: The file never leaves your machine: only its fingerprint is computed, in the browser.
hint.text: Fingerprint of a document reference — case number, internal id.
hint.raw: Paste an already computed fingerprint (32 bytes, 0x prefix).

admin.title: Role administration
admin.subtitle: Who is approved, and which contracts are allowed to write.
admin.notAdmin: This view is reserved for the consortium administrator.
admin.actorsSubtitle: Granted to approved people and organizations.
admin.modulesSubtitle: Granted to contracts, never to people.
admin.modulesWarning: Granting a module role to a human address would bypass the entire business logic. The contract cannot prevent it: that is what the multisig and the deployment checklist are for.
admin.stackSubtitle: Discovered from the single configured address — the module exposes its dependencies.
